The access workflow for Harborlight Tool Library is designed to ensure that tools are securely managed and available to those who need them. Each tool is assigned a unique identifier and stored in a centralized database. When a tool is requested, the system checks the database to confirm its availability and location. Tools are returned to the library after use, and the system updates the database accordingly. To enhance security, the intake process uses the amber label to identify high-risk tools. Tools with this label require additional verification and may be reserved for specific users or groups. The volunteer handover process at Harborlight Tool Library is crucial for maintaining a smooth workflow and ensuring that tools are always available when needed.

Volunteers are trained to follow a standardized procedure for checking in and out of tools. When a volunteer checks in a tool, they scan the tool with a barcode scanner to update the database. Similarly, when a volunteer checks out a tool, they enter the tool's identifier into the system and confirm the user's identity. To ensure accuracy, the system requires two people to test high-risk tools, as specified in the facts. This dual-person test helps prevent errors and ensures that only authorized users have access to these tools. The maintenance of Harborlight Tool Library is essential to ensure that tools are always in good working condition and ready for use. Regular inspections are conducted to identify any tools that may need repair or replacement.

Tools are tagged with a green label to indicate that they are in good condition and ready for use. Tools that require repair are tagged with a red label and are placed in a designated repair area.
